shortcut_name: three-vertex obstruction is exactly a triangle
evidence: The survivor searches for a pair and then a vertex "connected to both a and b", using "find smallest c > b connected to both a and b".
affordance_in_statement: if two sensors are linked by an interlock, they must not be active in the same phase ... find a specific structural failure: a subset of exactly three distinct sensors which, when considered in isolation, cannot possibly be assigned to the two phases
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task: three vertices are not 2-colorable exactly when all three pairwise interlocks exist. Avoiding this shortcut requires changing the requested obstruction to involve more than three vertices or otherwise changing the task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: It reduces the required three-sensor failure to finding a triangle and exploits ascending iteration to seek the lexicographically earliest one.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: a subset of exactly three distinct sensors ... cannot possibly be assigned to the two phases

common_affordance: A three-sensor subset violates two-phase assignment if and only if its three sensors form a triangle of pairwise interlocks.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The shown solution excerpt does not complete the search or produce output; after entering the loop it contains only a bare `m`.
It explicitly searches for a triangle in the complement graph, requiring the three pairs to be absent, whereas the invalid two-phase subset is a triangle in the interlock graph.
Although it searches for an interlock triangle, it scans edges in input order and prints every match, so it does not guarantee the lexicographically smallest single triple.

recommended_edit: No task-preserving edit can defeat the surviving approach, because the triangle characterization is intrinsic to exactly three vertices and two phases. Any effective edit must change the obstruction size or the assignment model.
regression_risk: Changing the task to a larger odd-cycle obstruction could accidentally make the already-defeated triangle-based implementations appear partially relevant again.
